s1.syndrome_frame: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Grossly edematous glans penis and corona
Tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar and granulation tissue
Inguinal lymphadenopathy
Systemic symptoms including fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite
key_facts: 78-year-old man presented with painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Symptoms duration of 1 month
Previous medical history included elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy
Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement
Routine blood test results were within normal limits
Cultures, assays, and blood tests evaluating for viral, bacterial, or fungal etiology were negative
Biopsy of the glans penis ulcer showed dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes
PCR analysis revealed a clonal IgH gene rearrangement
PET-CT scan demonstrated FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes

s4.champion: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

raw.champion: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
raw.rationale: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes that are CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, along with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, supports the diagnosis of a B-cell lymphoma. The fact that the lesion is localized to the skin and the patient has no other known sites of disease suggests a primary cutaneous lymphoma. The large cell morphology and the expression of CD20 and CD79a are most consistent with primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Mantle cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Mantle cell lymphoma typically involves the lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow, and is less likely to present as a solitary skin lesion.

rejected.label: Follicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Follicular lymphoma is typically a nodal disease and is less likely to present as a primary cutaneous lesion.

rejected.label: Marginal zone lymphoma
rejected.why: Marginal zone lymphoma can involve the skin, but the presence of CD5+ lymphocytes is not typical for this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Plasmablastic lymphoma
rejected.why: Plasmablastic lymphoma typically involves the oral cavity or other mucosal sites, and is less likely to present as a solitary skin lesion on the penis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The presence of CD20+ and CD79a+ lymphocytes suggests a B-cell lymphoma, rather than a T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma typically expresses CD30 and has a distinct morphological appearance, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: Lymphomatoid papulosis is a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma that typically presents with multiple papules or nodules, rather than a single ulcerative lesion.
